R/S\'s valuation framework (fair value and buy price)

R/S works out each company\'s fair (intrinsic) value by its sector. Banks, NBFCs and other financial companies: book value less net NPA (bad loans) per share, times the company\'s own median P/B of the last 3 years (the sector\'s when its history is short); with an ROA under 1%, no buy. Companies with machines and factories, like capital goods, auto, chemicals, construction and power: their own 3-year median EV/EBITDA × today\'s EBITDA, less debt, per share; with an ROCE under 12%, 20% less. Metals, mining, oil and gas: the same, but on the average (mid-cycle) EBITDA of the years, with a warning that a low P/E there is often peak earnings. IT, FMCG and pharma: PEG = P/E ÷ EPS\'s yearly growth over the last 3 years (forecasts of growth aren\'t free); under 1 cheap, over 2 dear; fair value = EPS × the company\'s own usual P/E, but no more than the P/E at PEG 2 (2 × growth). Other sectors, or with too little data: the older sector P/E–P/B and own-P/E method. Then penalties: the statutory auditor resigned in the last year −40%, debt over 1.5 times equity −20%, FII + DII stake down 3 quarters in a row −10%. Buy price = fair value × (1 − margin of safety): 20% for the top 100 companies by market value (large cap), 27.5% for 101–250 (mid cap) and 35% for the rest (small cap). Every company also gets a universal screen: promoters pledging over 15% of their shares means Reject (R/S \"Avoid\"); interest cover under 2.5 times means High Risk, and 3 years\' operating cash under 0.6 times the profit means doubtful earnings (either caps R/S at \"Caution\"). On the chart: price above the 200-day EMA and on an unfilled bullish FVG is the Buy Zone; this or last week the price went under a weekly swing low and closed back above is a weekly sweep. Price below the buy price, a weekly sweep and nothing holding it off is ⭐ the best chance. Opening a stock also looks at its news: volume 3 times the average or more but no filing or news in the last 3 days is a 🚩 Red Flag (could be an operator\'s game) and the framework holds off buying. Promoter pledges and auditor resignations come from NSE, so BSE-only stocks don\'t get these checks. The R/S card shows the fair value, buy price and flags, and \"The framework\'s full working\" shows every step. The new figures come as each stock\'s Screener page is read again, which will take a few days; until then some stocks stay on the older method. Not investment advice.
